title: What can a bookkeeper not do: defining professional scope of practice on Mac
metaTitle: What can a bookkeeper not do: scope of practice guide for Mac users
description: Learn what a bookkeeper can and cannot do to avoid scope creep, reduce liability, and build a sustainable practice on your Mac.
targetKeyword: what can a bookkeeper not do
intro: A bookkeeper cannot legally provide tax advice, perform audits, or sign off on financial statements unless they hold the appropriate certified accounting credentials. Knowing exactly what can a bookkeeper not do is the first step to protecting your license and your clients from costly compliance errors.
tldr: Bookkeepers manage day-to-day financial transactions, while accountants handle tax strategy and audits.
Scope creep occurs when you perform tasks outside your expertise, increasing your liability and risk.
Standardizing your service list and using clear engagement letters prevents confusion.
Lazur helps you organize your client communication and documentation to keep your scope clear.

blocks.text: Why defining your scope is hard

Clients often view bookkeeping as a commodity. They want a one-stop shop for every financial need. This pressure leads to scope creep. You might start by recording transactions, but soon you are asked to provide tax planning or investment advice. These tasks sit outside your professional scope. Accepting them without the right credentials creates massive liability. If you provide bad tax advice, you are responsible for the resulting penalties.
Common tasks outside the bookkeeper role

items: Signing off on financial statements or audits.
Providing formal tax advice or tax planning strategies.
Representing a client before the IRS or other tax authorities.
Making high-level investment or business strategy decisions.
Acting as the sole decision-maker for business expenditures.

blocks.text: When you use your Mac to manage client files, you must maintain strict data boundaries. Always check your employer or firm rules regarding client data access. If you use apps like Google Sheets or Excel, keep client-specific data in separate, restricted folders. Use ⌘ + Space to quickly find your files and ensure you are not mixing data across different client entities.
How to fix scope creep without spending money

items: Draft a clear engagement letter that lists exactly what you do.
Create a standard service menu for your clients to reference.
Update your SOPs to include a section on when to refer a client to a CPA.
Use your Mac Calendar to block out time for administrative tasks to avoid rushing.

blocks.text: The danger of manual entry and errors

Manual data entry is a primary driver of errors. When you spend 40% of your time typing, fatigue sets in. This is when mistakes happen. Use tools like the built-in macOS Text Replacement to speed up repetitive entries. Go to System Settings > Keyboard > Text Replacements. Add shortcuts for common account names or codes. This saves time and reduces the chance of typos.

faq.question: What is the main difference between a bookkeeper and an accountant?
faq.answer: A bookkeeper records financial transactions and maintains the ledger. An accountant analyzes those records to provide tax advice, financial planning, and audits.

faq.question: Can I provide tax advice if I am a bookkeeper?
faq.answer: No. Unless you are a licensed CPA or an Enrolled Agent, you should not provide formal tax advice. Always refer these questions to a qualified professional.

causes.title: Lack of defined engagement letters
causes.text: Without a written agreement, clients assume you provide all financial services.

causes.title: Fear of losing clients
causes.text: Bookkeepers often say yes to extra tasks because they worry about losing the client to a competitor.

causes.title: Misunderstanding of professional roles
causes.text: Many clients do not know the difference between a bookkeeper and a CPA.

fixes.title: Create a clear service menu
fixes.text: List exactly what you provide. Keep this document handy to show clients when they ask for extra help.

fixes.title: Referral network
fixes.text: Build a list of trusted CPAs to refer complex tax or strategy questions to immediately.

fixes.title: Standardize your workflow
fixes.text: Use templates for your emails and reports to ensure you stay within your established scope.
